subject: Civil Engineering
title: Reservoir Sedimentation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Reservoir Sedimentation.

hook.text: Every river carries sediment. When a dam stops the flow, sediment fills the reservoir.

buildup.text: Silt, sand, and clay settle behind the dam — slowly reducing water storage capacity year by year.

discovery.text: Some reservoirs lose 1-2% of capacity annually — within decades, they become useless.

twist.text: Flushing — opening low-level outlets during floods — can scour sediment out downstream.

climax.text: China's Sanmenxia Dam lost 90% of capacity to silt in just four years after completion.

punchline.text: Dams stop water — but they also stop sediment. That slow filling is their expiration date.

quiz.question: What happened to China's Sanmenxia Dam's capacity shortly after construction?
options: Earthquakes cracked the dam and reduced its structural capacity
Sediment filled 90% of the reservoir within four years
Drought reduced the river flow to unusable levels
